bibl.title: Short Chain Fatty Acids (SCFAs)-Mediated Gut Epithelial and Immune Regulation and Its Relevance for Inflammatory Bowel Diseases

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the short-chain fatty acids bacteria make from dietary fibre - acetate, propionate and butyrate - and what they do to the intestinal epithelium and immune cells in inflammatory bowel disease
span.quote: Here, we aim to provide an overview of microbial SCFAs production in the intestine and their effect on intestinal cells and the immune response. Moreover, gut microbiome changes in IBD are reviewed and how they are related to impaired intestinal SCFAs production and associate to cell metabolism and signaling pathways controlling mucosal homeostasis. Finally, the therapeutic potential of SCFAs for IBD will be discussed; either applied directly or through activation of SCFAs-producing bacteria by prebiotic or probiotic approaches.

span.label: whether the reduced SCFA levels seen in IBD are a mechanism of the disease and a possible therapy, or a consequence of it
span.quote: However, it remains unclear whether dysbiosis is a cause or a consequence of IBD

span.label: an overview of SCFA production, transport and receptor signalling in the gut, which states that fecal SCFA quantification measures a steady state and not production, and that whether dysbiosis causes IBD is unresolved
span.quote: Quantification of human intestinal SCFAs only provides steady state levels and may not accurately reflect the level of bacterial production as most SCFAs produced in the colonic lumen (90–95%) are absorbed by the gut mucosa

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Bacteroidetes (gram-negative) and Firmicutes (gram-positi ve) are the most abundant phyla in the intestine, with members of the Bacteroidetes mainly producing acetate and propionate, while Firmicutes mostly produce butyrate in the human gut

span.label: a bacterial metabolite acting as fuel, as a barrier signal and as an immunomodulator at once, whose measured concentration is the small fraction the mucosa did not absorb
span.quote: Bacteroidetes (gram-negative) and Firmicutes (gram-positi ve) are the most abundant phyla in the intestine, with members of the Bacteroidetes mainly producing acetate and propionate, while Firmicutes mostly produce butyrate in the human gut

span.label: a narrative review of germ-free and gnotobiotic models, antibiotic depletion, dietary fibre intervention, transporter and GPCR expression studies, and probiotic and prebiotic trials in UC and CD
span.term: a narrative review of germ-free and gnotobiotic models, antibiotic depletion, dietary fibre intervention, transporter and GPCR expression studies, and probiotic and prebiotic trials in UC and CD
span.quote: Here, we aim to provide an overview of microbial SCFAs production in the intestine and their effect on intestinal cells and the immune response. Moreover, gut microbiome changes in IBD are reviewed and how they are related to impaired intestinal SCFAs production and associate to cell metabolism and signaling pathways controlling mucosal homeostasis. Finally, the therapeutic potential of SCFAs for IBD will be discussed; either applied directly or through activation of SCFAs-producing bacteria by prebiotic or probiotic approaches.

span.label: 90 to 95 per cent of the SCFAs produced in the colonic lumen are taken up by the mucosa before anything is collected. A fecal SCFA concentration is therefore the small remainder, and a difference between patients and controls could be a difference in production, in absorption, or in transit - the number cannot distinguish them
span.term: the measurement is what absorption left behind
span.quote: Quantification of human intestinal SCFAs only provides steady state levels and may not accurately reflect the level of bacterial production as most SCFAs produced in the colonic lumen (90–95%) are absorbed by the gut mucosa

span.label: germ-free conditions make IL-10-deficient chronic colitis less severe and acute chemically-induced colitis worse. Any statement of the form 'the microbiota protects against colitis' is therefore incomplete without naming the model, and two papers reporting opposite results may both be right
span.term: an intervention whose sign is a property of the model
span.quote: This may go either way, e.g., IL-10 deficient mice show less severe chronic bowel inflammation in germfree (GF) conditions ( 13, 14), while acute chemically-induced colitis is exacerbated in GF mice compared to mice with a normal microbiome

span.label: probiotics showed no significant effect in Crohn's disease - and the review notes in the next sentence that the probiotics evaluated in those studies were not butyrate-producing bacteria. The hypothesis being tested was about butyrate and the intervention did not contain any
span.term: a null result whose treatment lacked the active ingredient
span.quote: So far, probiotic treatments have not shown a significant effect in inducing or maintaining remission of active or quiescent CD, or in preventing relapse of CD after surgically-induced remission (146, 147). However, probiotics evaluated in these studies were not butyrate-producing bacteria.

span.label: Bacteroidetes make acetate and propionate; Firmicutes make butyrate. A shift in phylum ratio is therefore automatically a shift in which metabolite the colon receives, which is why a compositional 16S result can be read as a functional claim and why that reading is only as good as the division
span.term: a division of labour that makes composition into chemistry
span.quote: Bacteroidetes (gram-negative) and Firmicutes (gram-positi ve) are the most abundant phyla in the intestine, with members of the Bacteroidetes mainly producing acetate and propionate, while Firmicutes mostly produce butyrate in the human gut

span.label: butyrate absorbed and oxidised by the epithelium consumes local oxygen. Deplete the anaerobes with antibiotics, butyrate falls, the mucosa stops consuming oxygen, and the colon becomes hospitable to aerobes such as Salmonella - a chain in which the metabolite acts by changing the physical environment rather than by signalling
span.quote: The susceptibility due to the depletion of anaerobic bacteria (induced by antibiotics ) is associated to a reduction in butyrate levels, thus promoting an aerobic environment and the expansion of aerobic bacteria suc h as Salmonella typhimurium

span.label: fecal and tissue SCFA quantification gives steady state levels and may not accurately reflect bacterial production, since 90-95% is absorbed by the mucosa
span.quote: Quantification of human intestinal SCFAs only provides steady state levels and may not accurately reflect the level of bacterial production as most SCFAs produced in the colonic lumen (90–95%) are absorbed by the gut mucosa

span.label: the fecal measurement is used as an approximation of gut levels, justified by association with resistant-starch diets rather than by direct comparison
span.quote: Nevertheless, the analysis of SCFAs in fecal samples is used as an approximation of gut levels, since excreted SCFA concentrati ons are associated with RS enriched diets (substrates of SCFAsproducing bacteria), inferring the relationship between in testinal SCFAs production and fecal levels

span.label: it remains unclear whether dysbiosis is a cause or a consequence of IBD
span.quote: However, it remains unclear whether dysbiosis is a cause or a consequence of IBD

span.label: the molecular mechanism by which SCFAs suppress pro-inflammatory mediators has not been completely determined in human or mouse mononuclear cell models
span.quote: The molecular mechanism involved in pro-inflammatory mediator suppression (e.g., LPS-induced chemokines and cytokines) by SCFAs has not been completely determined in other human/mouse mononuclear cell models

span.label: the mechanisms involved in IBD pathophysiology are still not resolved, nor how butyrate regulates inflammation and transcription in colonic mucosa
span.quote: The mechanisms involve d in IBD pathophysiology are still not resolved, nor how butyrat e regulates inflammation, influences metabolism and transcri ption in colonic mucosa.

span.label: well-controlled randomised placebo-controlled trials are still needed before prebiotic supplementation can be said to produce clinical improvement
span.quote: Nevertheless, well-controlled randomized place bocontrolled trials (RCT) are needed to fine tune a prebiotics supplementation plan to manage gastrointestinal tolerance in IBD patients, especially in CD, before rigorously confirming a n actual clinical improvement.

span.label: faecal microbiome transplantation has generated inconsistent results and is placed outside the scope of the review
span.quote: Such approaches may complement alternative strategies to modulate microbiota, such as fecal microbiome transplantation (FMT), which has generated inconsistent resul ts so far. As such, a detailed description of FMT is outside the scope of this review.

span.label: SCFA concentration is not one number - proximal colon runs 70-140 mM against 20-70 mM distally, and both depend on fibre intake
span.quote: SCFAs concentrations were found higher in proximal colon (around 70–140 mM) than distal colon (around 20–70 mM) in pigs, although this varies depending on the intake of DF

span.label: resistant-starch feeding trials in pigs, carried into human gut physiology as a model for dietary regulation of SCFA transporters
span.quote: Similar observations were made in pigs, where SLC16A1 mRNA levels increased in cecal and colonic mucosa after dietary supplementation with RS compared to digestible starch (DS) ( 41). In contrast, SLC5A8 mRNA levels (encoding SMCT1) were not affected by RS or DS diet ( 41), showing a specific regulation of MCT1 expression by RS in comparison to SMCT1

span.label: the Codex Alimentarius definition of dietary fibre, a food-regulation standard used here to fix what counts as the substrate
span.quote: Here, we aim to provide an overview of microbial SCFAs production in the intestine and their effect on intestinal cells and the immune response. Moreover, gut microbiome changes in IBD are reviewed and how they are related to impaired intestinal SCFAs production and associate to cell metabolism and signaling pathways controlling mucosal homeostasis. Finally, the therapeutic potential of SCFAs for IBD will be discussed; either applied directly or through activation of SCFAs-producing bacteria by prebiotic or probiotic approaches.

span.label: SLC5A8 (SMCT1) mRNA measured alongside SLC16A1 (MCT1) in the same pigs on the same resistant-starch and digestible-starch diets
span.note: eliminates: a general effect of diet on monocarboxylate transport - SMCT1 does not move, so the MCT1 response is specific to that transporter · outcome: held
span.quote: Similar observations were made in pigs, where SLC16A1 mRNA levels increased in cecal and colonic mucosa after dietary supplementation with RS compared to digestible starch (DS) ( 41). In contrast, SLC5A8 mRNA levels (encoding SMCT1) were not affected by RS or DS diet ( 41), showing a specific regulation of MCT1 expression by RS in comparison to SMCT1

span.label: germ-free conditions applied in two different colitis models - chronic IL-10-deficient and acute chemically-induced
span.note: eliminates: a single-model answer standing for the microbiota's role - running both shows the sign reverses, which one model alone would have hidden · outcome: partial
span.quote: This may go either way, e.g., IL-10 deficient mice show less severe chronic bowel inflammation in germfree (GF) conditions ( 13, 14), while acute chemically-induced colitis is exacerbated in GF mice compared to mice with a normal microbiome

span.label: SCFA levels measured in liver and blood as well as intestine
span.note: eliminates: the assumption that SCFA action is systemic - levels elsewhere are much lower, placing signalling and uptake at the mucosa, while their detectability still supports systemic function · outcome: held
span.quote: Finally, SCFAs levels in other tissues such as liver or blood ( Table 1) are much lower than in the intestine ( 42), demonstrating that SCFAs signaling, uptake and/or metaboli sm mainly occur at the intestinal mucosa. However, detection of extra intestinal levels implies that these metabolites ha ve systemic functions, as established for central nervous sys tem autoimmunity

span.label: SCFA-producing bacteria and SCFA levels both measured in IBD patients, rather than inferring the metabolite from the taxon
span.note: eliminates: a taxonomic shift being reported as a metabolic one - here both the producers and the product are shown to be reduced · outcome: held
span.quote: Importantly, IBD patients not only show reduced levels of dominant SCFAs-producing bacteria (like Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Roseburia intestinalis ) in intestinal mucosa and feces, but the actual steady state levels of SCFAs herein also appear to be lower compared to healthy controls

span.label: probiotic trials in Crohn's disease, reported as showing no significant effect on inducing or maintaining remission
span.note: eliminates: nothing about butyrate, and the review says so in the next sentence - the probiotics tested were not butyrate-producing bacteria, so the null result does not test the mechanism it appears to test · outcome: failed
span.quote: So far, probiotic treatments have not shown a significant effect in inducing or maintaining remission of active or quiescent CD, or in preventing relapse of CD after surgically-induced remission (146, 147). However, probiotics evaluated in these studies were not butyrate-producing bacteria.

span.label: well-controlled randomised placebo-controlled trials of prebiotic supplementation, named as needed and not yet done
span.note: eliminates: placebo response and spontaneous remission in IBD - the randomised placebo-controlled trials that would rule them out are named as needed and not yet done · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: Nevertheless, well-controlled randomized place bocontrolled trials (RCT) are needed to fine tune a prebiotics supplementation plan to manage gastrointestinal tolerance in IBD patients, especially in CD, before rigorously confirming a n actual clinical improvement.

span.label: faecal microbiome transplantation, named as producing inconsistent results and excluded from the review's scope
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that the SCFA effects are reproduced by wholesale microbiota transfer - excluded from the review's scope rather than resolved · outcome: absent-stated-about-other
span.quote: Such approaches may complement alternative strategies to modulate microbiota, such as fecal microbiome transplantation (FMT), which has generated inconsistent resul ts so far. As such, a detailed description of FMT is outside the scope of this review.
